item.title: The chemistry of the interstellar medium
item.description:
The interstellar medium#

In all galaxies, the space between celestial bodies is filled with a collection of gas and dust particles. These particles are known as interstellar medium (ISM) and possesses density of $10^{-9}$ grains$\times$cm$^{-3}$.\citep{wakelamrev} The ISM plays an important role as a reservoir of constituents for the formation of new stars. ISM is mostly composed of hydrogen atoms and they are used to measure the relative abundances of the other elements. The second most common element is helium with a relative abundance of 8.5$\times 10^{-2}$ per hydrogen atom, followed by oxygen (2.6$\times 10^{-4}$per hydrogen atom\citep{Markwick_2000}) and carbon (1.2$\times 10^{-4}$ \citep{cardelli_1993} per hydrogen atom). All other elements are present with abundances lower than $10^{-4}$.
